_comment: Workflows whose RED IS THEIR OUTPUT, not their failure. A detector reports a
condition; while the condition holds it exits non-zero, and that is the
design. scripts/watch-silently-dead-crons.mjs lists these separately instead
of calling them dead — without this it would report them every day forever,
and a watch that cries wolf is how odds-backfill.yml went fifteen days
AN ENTRY HERE IS NOT AN EXCUSE. Each names the condition it reports and the
document tracking it. The watch still prints how long each has been red, so
a detector red for months stays visible rather than becoming furniture.
Adding an entry to silence a genuinely broken workflow is the abuse this
file makes easy to spot in review: the reason has to be written down.
KEYS ARE REPO-QUALIFIED as of 2026-09-17, when the watch widened from one
repo to four. `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` exists in all four; a bare path
key would let a declaration made for one repo excuse a genuinely dead cron
of the same name in another. The form is `owner/repo:.github/workflows/x.yml`.

2026-09-19: undeployed-src-watch.yml was the third workflow the dead-cron watch flagged that day and it is DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED HERE. Its red is caused by a fixable repo defect — the provenance census writes a regenerated ROUTE_PROVENANCE_GENERATED_AT into src/route-provenance.js while carrying the skip directive, so it bumps a deploy-trigger path and suppresses the deploy that would clear it. Declaring it would suppress the one signal that reports a genuinely undeployed src change, which is the abuse the paragraph above describes. Fix the cause, do not declare the symptom.
